subject: psychiatry
title: Phencyclidine, Inhalants, Nicotine, and Anticholinergic Poisoning

steps.tx: **Phencyclidine**, widely known as PCP or angel dust, operates pharmacologically as a non-competitive antagonist at the glutamate NMDA receptor complex. Acute intoxication produces a notorious clinical state characterized by unpredictable violent agitation, superhuman muscular strength, analgesia, blank stare, severe ataxia, and acute psychosis.
steps.say: Phencyclidine blocks NMDA receptors, provoking violent agitation, anesthesia, and unpredictable rage with loss of pain sensation.

left.title: Behavioral Presentation
points: Apparent 'superhuman' strength and insensitivity to pain
Catatonic posturing or bizarre blank staring

right.title: Objective Physical Signs
points: Risk of fatal rhabdomyolysis and renal failure

steps.tx: **Rotary and vertical nystagmus** stands as the pathognomonic physical examination sign of phencyclidine intoxication, rarely observed in other substance toxicities. The presence of multidirectional rotary nystagmus paired with marked motor ataxia and extreme behavioral agitation strongly confirms PCP toxicity over standard psychostimulant intoxication.
steps.say: Rotary and vertical nystagmus is pathognomonic for phencyclidine poisoning, distinguishing it from amphetamine or cocaine toxicity.

steps.tx: **Inhalant abuse** involves the deliberate sniffing or huffing of volatile hydrocarbons, such as toluene, benzene, butane, glue, and aerosol paint solvents, predominantly among impoverished adolescents. Inhaled vapors produce rapid intoxication, slurred speech, and ataxia, but carry lethal risk of sudden sniffing death syndrome from fatal ventricular arrhythmias.
steps.say: Inhalant abuse involves sniffing glue or paint fumes. It carries lethal risk of sudden sniffing death syndrome due to ventricular fibrillation.

nodes.label: Volatile hydrocarbon inhalation via plastic bag or rag ('huffing')
Rapid lipid-soluble diffusion into central nervous system
Myocardial sensitization to circulating endogenous catecholamines
Sudden sniffing death: acute stress triggers fatal ventricular fibrillation

steps.tx: **Nicotine dependence neurobiology** centers on nicotine binding to presynaptic alpha-4 beta-2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in the ventral tegmental area, triggering burst firing and rapid dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens. Chronic smoking up-regulates nicotinic receptors, precipitating intense withdrawal cravings, irritability, and restlessness within hours of cessation.
steps.say: Nicotine binds alpha-4 beta-2 receptors in the midbrain, releasing dopamine. Withdrawal produces severe cravings, irritability, and restlessness within hours.

left.title: Nicotine Pharmacodynamics
points: Rapid arterial delivery to brain within ten seconds
Surge of dopamine in nucleus accumbens

right.title: Withdrawal Syndrome
points: Onset within two hours of last cigarette
Bradycardia, increased appetite, and weight gain

steps.tx: **Varenicline** is a high-affinity partial agonist at alpha-4 beta-2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, recognized as the most effective single smoking cessation monotherapy. By partially stimulating receptors, varenicline alleviates withdrawal cravings; by competitively blocking nicotine from binding, it eliminates the rewarding satisfaction of slip cigarettes.
steps.say: Varenicline is a partial agonist at alpha-4 beta-2 nicotinic receptors, relieving withdrawal while blocking smoking satisfaction.

vis.title: Smoking Cessation Therapies
rows: Dry mouth, insomnia; lowers seizure threshold
Local skin erythema, vivid dreams if worn overnight

steps.tx: **Nicotine replacement therapy**, abbreviated NRT, delivers controlled, clean medicinal nicotine without the lethal combustion carcinogens, carbon monoxide, or tar present in tobacco smoke. Combining a long-acting transdermal nicotine patch for baseline craving suppression with short-acting gum or lozenges for breakthrough cravings yields significantly higher cessation rates.
steps.say: Combining a continuous transdermal nicotine patch with short-acting nicotine gum provides superior cessation rates compared to monotherapy.

nodes.label: Apply transdermal patch (21 mg/day) upon waking for steady baseline coverage
Use 2 mg or 4 mg nicotine gum for acute situational breakthrough cravings
Chew gum slowly until peppery taste emerges, then park in buccal cheek
Taper patch dose sequentially to 14 mg then 7 mg over twelve weeks

steps.tx: **Dhatura poisoning and anticholinergic delirium** arises from ingestion of Dhatura stramonium seeds containing tropane belladonna alkaloids (hyoscyamine, scopolamine, atropine), which competitively antagonize central and peripheral muscarinic acetylcholine receptors. Delirium presents with purposeless carphologia, micropsia, and severe combativeness, demanding rapid gastric decontamination and definitive antidote administration.
steps.say: Dhatura poisoning blocks muscarinic receptors, causing anticholinergic delirium with picking movements, dilated pupils, and fever.

vis.title: Classic Anticholinergic Toxidrome
rows: Blockade of muscarinic sweat and salivary glands

steps.tx: **Physostigmine antidote** is a tertiary amine carbamate that reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase, raising acetylcholine concentrations to outcompete atropine at muscarinic synapses. Unlike quaternary neostigmine, physostigmine crosses the blood-brain barrier into the central nervous system, reversing both life-threatening peripheral arrhythmias and agitated central anticholinergic delirium.
steps.say: Physostigmine is the tertiary amine antidote for dhatura poisoning, crossing into the brain to reverse central anticholinergic delirium.

left.title: Physostigmine (Tertiary Amine)
points: Administered slow IV 1 to 2 mg over five minutes

right.title: Neostigmine (Quaternary Amine)
points: Permanent positive charge blocks BBB crossing
Used strictly for peripheral neuromuscular reversal
